transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-01 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee, Maya Patel (Redwood); Carlos Medina, Priya Iyer, Ethan Cho (StratusHub)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for a Redwood-embedded offering in StratusHub Marketplace, and joint solution packaging (billing/SKU mapping, onboarding flow). Primary topics: marketplace artifact checklist, network and security (VPC peering, KMS), deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and next steps for a reference arch draft and pilot scoping.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing checklist and assets
- Reference architecture (network, auth, routing)
- Integration touchpoints: SSO, audit logs, billing mapping
- Pilot scope and benchmarks (latency, throughput)

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll get started. I'm Jordan from Redwood, our SE Maya and I are here. Thanks Carlos, Priya, Ethan for squeezing this in.
[00:00:12] Carlos Medina: yeah thanks, glad to be here. we want to make sure our marketplace listing is, like, straight forward and that the integration pattern won't surprise our customers.
[00:00:25] Maya Patel: great, quick agenda: checklist for listing, RA options, networking and security, then pilot / next steps. if that works for you we can jump in.
[00:00:38] Ethan Cho: sounds good. one thing - we do have a few enterprise customers asking about private deployments and compliance, so we'll want that covered.
[00:00:48] Jordan Lee: noted; we'll cover hosted, dedicated and private (VPC/on-prem). ok first, marketplace assets - Carlos, what's StratusHub's minimal artifact set?
[00:01:02] Carlos Medina: usually we need a listing doc, logo, marketing blurb, pricing tiers, obviously technical integration notes, and an RA for customers. also sample IaC templates if possible.
[00:01:16] Jordan Lee: perfect - Redwood can provide a marketplace checklist doc, an RA template, and IaC snippets for quickstart. Maya will own the RA diagrams.
[00:01:29] Maya Patel: yes, i'll put together diagrams for three flows: 1) Redwood hosted (Redwood API + managed model endpoints), 2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU on our infra), and 3) Private (VPC peering / on-prem). each will have network, auth, and data flow lines.
[00:01:44] Priya Iyer: quick clarifying q - for the private flow, do you expect us to host the control plane or is it customer-managed?
[00:01:53] Maya Patel: good question. we have an option: customer can run a private control plane in their VPC (we call Redwood Private) or we can offer a hybrid where control plane is in Redwood but data plane resides in customer VPC. for marketplace listing we should document both.
[00:02:09] Ethan Cho: for our customers, hybrid is preferred because they like not managing the control plane but want data residency.
[00:02:17] Jordan Lee: noted. next, security and compliance - what proofs do you require to list?
[00:02:24] Carlos Medina: SOC 2 type 2 attestation, encryption details (KMS/HSM), SSO/SAML support, audit logs, and data handling guarantees. also clear SLAs.
[00:02:36] Jordan Lee: we have SOC 2, can share the attestation. we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and we have audit logs and RBAC. i'll send the security checklist after the call.
[00:02:48] Priya Iyer: can you outline KMS integration? specifically for the hybrid model - how does key management work?
[00:02:56] Maya Patel: for hybrid we can either integrate with your KMS via an IAM role so Redwood can encrypt at rest with customer keys, or with Private deployment you bring KMS completely into your account. there are small operational items around rotation and CMKs.
[00:03:12] Carlos Medina: ok great. next, network - we need the VPC peering steps and egress considerations.
[00:03:20] Maya Patel: we'll include sample peering configs. important detail: for Dedicated we typically peer and use private subnets; for hosted we provide secure endpoints over TLS and optional VPC endpoints. KV cache and model weights never traverse public endpoints in the private flow.
[00:03:36] Priya Iyer: i'm hearing KV cash instead of KV cache in a few docs we've seen - haha, minor transcription quirk but pls ensure docs use "KV cache".
[00:03:45] Maya Patel: will do.
[00:03:49] Jordan Lee: on billing and marketplace SKU mapping - StratusHub, how do you expect the metering to work? per-token? per-instance? monthly commit?
[00:03:59] Carlos Medina: we support multiple patterns; marketplace prefers clear SKUs. ideal for Redwood would be a per-seat or per-unit marketplace SKU plus a usage metric we can pass. many ISVs do monthly commit for Dedicated.
[00:04:14] Jordan Lee: Redwood offers usage-based for hosted (per-token/per-embedding) and reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated. for marketplace listing we'll provide SKU options and recommended mappings. Maya, we'll need a short doc describing the SKU mapping.
[00:04:27] Maya Patel: i'll draft the mapping and include suggested pricing bands.
[00:04:32] Ethan Cho: on the billing front, are there any technical requirements for metering endpoints? like specific reporting APIs?
[00:04:41] Jordan Lee: we can emit usage logs with agreed schema; we also integrate with marketplace billing via a metering API. we'll share the schema.
[00:04:50] Carlos Medina: good. next, performance and pilot benchmarks - some of our customers care about latency under 100ms for short prompts.
[00:04:59] Maya Patel: that's a tight SLO for full-gen models; with Redwood hosted on optimized kernels and batching we can hit 50-150ms median for small models but for larger seq lengths it's higher. for Dedicated we can tune instance types. we'll include perf profiles in the RA.
[00:05:16] Priya Iyer: can you run a benchmark in our region (us-west-2) as part of pilot?
[00:05:23] Jordan Lee: yes, pilot can include a benchmark run. it'll need sample traffic pattern and model selection; maya will coordinate.
[00:05:31] Maya Patel: i'll need sample prompts, desired percentiles, and the region/instance preference.
[00:05:38] Carlos Medina: we'll provide.
[00:05:42] Jordan Lee: technical deep-dive - auth flows: SSO/SAML for UI, and token-based API auth for service traffic. do you require SCIM?
[00:05:52] Ethan Cho: SCIM for user provisioning would be nice but not a blocker for initial listing.
[00:05:58] Maya Patel: ok we'll document SAML/SSO and optional SCIM.
[00:06:04] Priya Iyer: regarding logs and audit, retention is a requirement for some customers; can we specify retention windows?
[00:06:10] Jordan Lee: Redwood Console supports configurable retention tiers as an add-on; we'll document default retention and options.
[00:06:17] Carlos Medina: good. on packaging - StratusHub wants a "one-click" marketplace install that provisions a connector and onboarding flow. how much of that can Redwood automate?
[00:06:27] Maya Patel: we can provide a CloudFormation/Terraform template that provisions the connector and sets up the peering and SNS for billing. the one-click experience can kick off a provisioning job on our side. we'll need some metadata from StratusHub for the integration in your console.
[00:06:41] Ethan Cho: perfect, and for the listing page we need a short 2-3 minute demo video; can Redwood provide an explainer?
[00:06:49] Jordan Lee: yes, we can produce a short demo and a quickstart video.
[00:06:53]
[00:07:00] Maya Patel: quick note on model catalog mapping - StratusHub customers may want to choose open models vs commercial. Redwood's model catalog has curated profiles per model and recommended quantization profiles; we'll include mapping to the models you plan to surface.
[00:07:16] Priya Iyer: do you provide model version pinning and rollout policies?
[00:07:20] Maya Patel: yes, version pinning and canary rollouts, A/B testing and automatic fallback to cheaper variants if needed. that's useful to call out in the RA.
[00:07:29] Carlos Medina: awesome. any security caveats about KV cache or prefix caching we should call out?
[00:07:35] Maya Patel: prefix/KV caching can be disabled for sensitive workloads; also caching is tenant-aware and encrypted. but be explicit in RA for customers who have strict isolation needs.
[00:07:46] Ethan Cho: on the private/on-prem option - what's the deployment model? containerized appliance? helm chart?
[00:07:54] Maya Patel: we provide an on-prem package with Helm charts for Kubernetes, or an appliance image for air-gapped environments. for marketplace we'd list the helm chart + operator steps.
[00:08:04] Priya Iyer: any special hardware reqs for on-prem? GPUs?
[00:08:08] Maya Patel: yes, for inference with high throughput 16+GB GPU class is recommended; we list supported instance types in RA. for lighter workloads CPU-only is possible but latency and cost differ.
[00:08:19] Jordan Lee: ok, circling back to pilot: timeline? StratusHub: what cadence do you want?
[00:08:26] Carlos Medina: we'd like a 4-week pilot: week 1 - onboarding + peering, week 2 - smoke tests & metering, week 3 - perf run, week 4 - wrap and go/no-go.
[00:08:37] Jordan Lee: sounds reasonable; we'll propose a statement of work after this.
[00:08:42] Maya Patel: action items - i'll draft RA, jordan will send security docs, and priya will send network info.
[00:08:50] Priya Iyer: yes will do.
[00:08:54]
[00:09:10] Jordan Lee: quick question from the SE side - do you have any constraints around regional data residency? specific regions you want prioritized?
[00:09:19] Carlos Medina: initially us-west-2 and eu-west-1; we'll expand later.
[00:09:24] Maya Patel: we'll include region notes and preferred availability zones in the RA.
[00:09:30] Ethan Cho: what about support model? marketplace customers expect first-line support from StratusHub. do you want Redwood to white-label support or share escalations?
[00:09:40] Jordan Lee: we typically do a co-support model: partner handles first-line, Redwood handles backline escalations. we'll provide runbooks for common issues.
[00:09:50] Carlos Medina: ok.
[00:09:52] Maya Patel: small gotcha we've seen - marketplace listing screenshots must not show internal IPs or customer data; ensure demo accounts are scrubbed.
[00:10:02] Priya Iyer: noted.
[00:10:06] Jordan Lee: any questions on monitoring / observability?
[00:10:10] Priya Iyer: do you export traces or metrics that we can ingest in our platform?
[00:10:14] Maya Patel: yes we export metrics and traces (OpenTelemetry friendly). we'll provide an example ingestion pipeline and dashboard tiles you can embed.
[00:10:24] Carlos Medina: good.
[00:10:26] Jordan Lee: alright, let's do a quick run through of the artifacts we'll share: marketplace checklist, RA diagrams, IaC templates, security checklist, demo video, and billing mapping. anything to add?
[00:10:38] Priya Iyer: add sample peering config and service account details.
[00:10:42] Jordan Lee: added.
[00:10:44] Ethan Cho: in terms of internal approvals on our side we'll need legal to review the SLA and some of the data residency statements.
[00:10:52] Jordan Lee: understood; we'll flag those sections in the RA and checklist.
[00:10:57] Maya Patel: one more technical note - for the hybrid mode routing policies, Redwood's smart router can direct requests based on latency, cost or region; we can pre-configure defaults for StratusHub customers to simplify.
[00:11:10] Carlos Medina: good to know.
[00:11:13]
[00:11:40] Priya Iyer: quick call-out: for the pilot we'll need an SLA doc stub to share, even if provisional.
[00:11:46] Jordan Lee: i'll send a draft SLA as part of the security pack.
[00:11:50] Maya Patel: also i'll include the recommended quantization/sequence length profiles for models to hit the latency targets you mentioned.
[00:11:59] Ethan Cho: how will updates to the RA be versioned? we often want to track changes for customers.
[00:12:05] Jordan Lee: we'll provide a versioned RA in your partner repo and tag releases; the marketplace listing will reference a specific RA version.
[00:12:13] Carlos Medina: ok.
[00:12:16] Jordan Lee: any blockers we haven't covered?
[00:12:19] Carlos Medina: not at the moment. maybe one minor thing - can you provide a stub listing copy for legal review?
[00:12:26] Jordan Lee: yes, stub listing copy + marketing blurb will be in the assets pack.
[00:12:31]
[00:12:40] Maya Patel: i'll also add a short troubleshooting runbook for common install failures.
[00:12:45] Priya Iyer: helpful.
[00:12:48] Jordan Lee: great. looks like we're aligned. I'll recap next steps at the end.
[00:12:55] Carlos Medina: thanks.
[00:13:00]
[00:13:30] Jordan Lee: recap: Jordan to send security checklist, stub SLA, and demo video plan; Maya to deliver RA diagram, IaC template, and perf profile; Priya to send VPC details and preferred regions; StratusHub to pick pilot customers and timelines. we'll set a follow-up for 1 week to review RA draft.
[00:13:52] Priya Iyer: confirmed.
[00:13:55] Ethan Cho: confirmed.
[00:13:58] Jordan Lee: perfect. any final q's?
[00:14:02] Carlos Medina: none. thanks everyone.
[00:14:06] Jordan Lee: thanks all - end call.
